endpoint: forebrain epileptiform event frequency (interictal and ictal-like) in agar-immobilised larva
action_on_target: GABA-A positive modulation (diazepam, stiripentol), mixed or unresolved (valproate, KBr)
control: same-fish baseline, 7 fish per drug; no target-specific control
effect_note: event frequency and fraction of time seizing fell; burst DURATION did not change; no sedation test on this panel
locator_quote: Epileptiform event frequency ... were reduced by valproate, diazepam, potassium bromide and stiripentol
transfer_conditions: Supports a positive-modulator benzodiazepine class (clobazam-like) as one of few classes that move network discharge in a LoF developmental epilepsy; developing nervous system; spontaneous discharge
transfer_breakers: 1 mM bath in immobilised larva is not a plasma-range exposure; GABA-A drive in zebrafish forebrain at 5 dpf may differ from mammalian cortex; clobazam itself not tested here

action_on_target: T-type calcium channel blockade (assumed class action)
control: same-fish baseline; 7 fish
effect_note: epileptiform activity became MORE frequent in 4 of 7 fish; no benefit in the other fish; the repository ETX-in-pup result (Cheng 2020) has no counterpart here
locator_quote: ethosuximide (4 of 7 fish) or vigabatrin (6 of 7 fish)
transfer_conditions: The Dravet-type fish is a pharmacoresistant LoF model; ETX failing here is a negative for generalising ETX to LoF developmental networks
transfer_breakers: Cheng 2020 reports ETX efficacy against PTZ only in Wwox-/- pups; a PTZ-provoked pup and a spontaneous-discharge larva are different endpoints; Scn1a LoF is interneuron-driven, which WWOX loss may or may not share

control: same-fish baseline; 7 fish
effect_note: activity more frequent in 6 of 7 fish; vigabatrin is NOT neutral here, it worsened it
locator_quote: ethosuximide (4 of 7 fish) or vigabatrin (6 of 7 fish)
transfer_conditions: Repository carries vigabatrin as a GABA-axis agent; this is the only direct network test of it in a LoF DEE model found here and it is adverse
transfer_breakers: Vigabatrin works in TSC (D25); an agent can be adverse in LoF channelopathy and favourable in mTOR-driven disease, so sign does not transfer by drug alone

control: same-fish baseline; 7 fish
effect_note: activity more frequent in 2 of 7 fish; matches the clinical and mouse pro-convulsant pattern of sodium-channel blockers in Scn1a loss
locator_quote: epileptiform activity became more frequent following exposure to carbamazepine
transfer_conditions: Pro-convulsant sodium-channel-block pattern is a LoF-interneuron property; WWOX bursting has been linked to reduced inhibition (Breton 2021 via IT14 P3), so it is a plausible hazard class
transfer_breakers: Whether WWOX loss lowers Nav1.1-dependent interneuron output is unmeasured; only 2 of 7 fish

endpoint: electrographic burst discharge in larva (field electrode, forebrain)
action_on_target: T-type calcium channel block (class action, not shown here)
cell_type_or_stage: 5 dpf larva; library screen then EEG
stress_or_context: spontaneous seizures; first-stage locomotion hit, second-stage EEG
control: two independent locomotion trials, then field recording; WT swim distance unchanged (no sedation signal at 500 uM)
effect_note: 1 of 1012 repurposed compounds that passed behaviour AND suppressed electrographic bursts; the other 3 locomotion hits were false positives with ongoing discharge
locator_quote: suppressed burst discharge activity in scn1Lab mutant larvae
transfer_conditions: The only T-type-class compound confirmed on discharge in a LoF DEE network; gives INV-03 a direction in a developmental LoF model
transfer_breakers: Authors themselves note ethosuximide and flunarizine were not similarly effective, and dimethadione also blocks hERG; so T-type attribution is not supported

intervention: ethosuximide; flunarizine; phenytoin; carbamazepine; decimemide; tiletamine; primidone; phenacemide; vigabatrin
action_on_target: T-type block (ETX, flunarizine); sodium-channel block; NMDAR antagonism (tiletamine); GABA-T inhibition
control: not applicable (class statement from prior and current assays)
effect_note: listed by the authors as ineffective; this is a statement that the model is resistant to at least eight ASMs
locator_quote: resistant to many antiepileptic compounds (e.g., phenytoin, carbamazepine, ethosuximide
transfer_conditions: Resistance pattern resembles Dravet and many DEEs; relevant if WWOX-DEE is also drug-resistant
transfer_breakers: Statement summarises earlier work; per-drug data for most not shown in this paper

action_on_target: NMDA receptor channel block (tiletamine; huperzine A also AChE inhibition)
stress_or_context: spontaneous seizures; huperzine A also tested in WT PTZ
control: WT larvae in PTZ: huperzine A was effective there, not in scn1lab mutants
effect_note: huperzine A failed in the mutant but worked in acute PTZ WT fish: a general-anticonvulsant signal in a provoked model did not transfer to the LoF channelopathy; tiletamine listed as ineffective (also toxic in the 100 uM library pass)
locator_quote: huperzine A failed to significantly alter scn1Lab seizure behavior at any concentration tested
transfer_conditions: Direct contrast between a provoked-seizure WT result and a genetic-LoF spontaneous model; the NMDAR antagonist class (INV-04 sibling thread) is not corroborated
transfer_breakers: Excitatory-gain mechanism in WWOX (d-APV-sensitive slice bursts) is different from a sodium-channel LoF interneuron lesion

intervention: mepivacaine and other library compounds scored hyperexcitable (55 compounds)
control: baseline of the same larva
effect_note: mepivacaine raised swim activity; 55 compounds were hyperexcitable or pro-convulsant and 154 toxic out of 1012
locator_quote: mepivacaine, a hyperexcitable proconvulsant anesthetic
transfer_conditions: Gives a screen-level estimate of the hazard rate: pro-convulsant or toxic outcomes are about 20 percent of a repurposed library in this LoF network
transfer_breakers: Locomotion is a behavioural readout of a hyperkinetic state, not proven seizure; no electrographic confirmation for these

endpoint: locomotion (and EEG at the end of Dinday 2015) after dosing
control: locomotion plus field recording in the same fish; 1 mM was toxic
effect_note: electrographic seizures suppressed to control level at the high tested concentration, only partial at the lower one; the window to toxicity is narrow
locator_quote: The fenfluramine-treated scn1Lab mutant exhibited a suppression of spontaneous electrographic seizure discharge to levels similar to controls
transfer_conditions: Gives serotonin-axis agents a LoF-DEE precedent; fenfluramine clinical benefit in Dravet matches
transfer_breakers: Fish effect not reproduced in Scn1a A1783V mouse hyperthermia (D17); concentration window to lethality is narrow

action_on_target: 5-HT2B receptor agonism (binding preference; agonism for the known ligands)
control: receptor binding profiling (blinded, PDSP); inactive analogues with 5-HT2B binding exist (5 and 14); no antagonist-reversal or genetic control
effect_note: electrographic event frequency reduced; two 2B-selective analogues did not work, so binding alone does not predict effect; authors say mechanism needs molecular strategies
locator_quote: Three 5-HT 2B R agonists, methylergonovine, 6-APB and norfenfluramine suppressed convulsive swim behaviours in a concentration-dependent manner
transfer_conditions: Neuromodulatory (serotonergic) class acting on a network without ion-channel gene dependence; WWOX reduction of inhibition could be partly compensated
transfer_breakers: Attribution rests on correlation of binding and effect; 5-HT2B agonism carries valvulopathy liability (clinical, not tested here)

control: dose-response, 30 and 90 min
effect_note: biphasic dose response, so direction depends on concentration; Ro60-0175 only borderline; TL-99 inactive
locator_quote: CP-809, 101 gave a biphasic response, as did m-CPP, the active metabolite of trazodone
transfer_conditions: Warns that serotonergic class results are non-monotonic in this assay
transfer_breakers: Shown only in swim velocity; apomorphine increased velocity like WT, so dopaminergic confounding exists

endpoint: ictal-like event frequency, local field recording of midbrain, 4 dpf larva
action_on_target: sodium-channel block; mixed; T-type block; SV2A; GABA-A positive modulation
stress_or_context: spontaneous ictal-like events, about 7.6 per 15 min

locator_quote: No statistically significant changes in event frequency were noted for any of the five ASMs tested

transfer_breakers: Single concentration, single time point; only one paralog (stxbp1b) with a viable phenotype; no sedation measurement

control: within-fish baseline, n 11 and 14; no target-specific control
effect_note: 80 and 83 percent reduction (6.5 to 1.3; 8.2 to 1.4 events per 15 min); serotonergic compounds work across two LoF DEE zebrafish models, while the ASMs of D12 do not
locator_quote: Event frequencies were significantly reduced following exposure to clemizole (Figures 3A,B ) and trazodone
transfer_conditions: Cross-model replication of a non-ion-channel class; a candidate whose direction survives a change of lesion
transfer_breakers: Same laboratory and same assay as D09-D11; high bath concentration; not independent replication

system: stxbp1b LoF larva (discharge); stxbp1a LoF larva (locomotion deficit, not hyperexcitability)
stress_or_context: spontaneous ictal-like events; separate movement-deficit endpoint
control: within-fish baseline; p 0.86 for event frequency
effect_note: no change in discharge; the movement-deficit endpoint in stxbp1a is hypo-activity and is NOT the hyperexcitability endpoint, kept apart
locator_quote: we observed no change in seizure event frequency during a 60 min 4‐PBA
transfer_conditions: Shows that a proteostasis-class agent (relevant to the repository chaperone thread) does not reduce discharge in a LoF DEE network
transfer_breakers: Rescue on movement deficit was also absent; this speaks to 4-PBA, not to chaperones as a class

endpoint: hyperthermia seizure threshold (core temperature) in 5 to 7 week mice
control: vehicle and carbamazepine arms in the same cohorts; cross-over

transfer_conditions: Corroborates clobazam as a threshold-raising agent in a developmental LoF mouse; N-desmethylclobazam not separately tested
transfer_breakers: Endpoint is a provoked threshold, not spontaneous discharge; plasma levels not matched to human; clobazam plus valproate failed in D16

endpoint: hyperthermia seizure threshold; spontaneous seizure frequency (video-EEG)
intervention: clobazam plus valproate; add-on stiripentol (14-day food and pump exposure)
action_on_target: GABA-A positive modulation; mixed; GABA-A modulation and metabolism interference
control: control pellet; clobazam plus valproate arm; plasma and brain concentrations measured

locator_quote: CLB + VPA treatment failed to increase the seizure threshold temperatures in Scn1a A1783V/WT mice on Days 7 and 14
transfer_conditions: Subchronic exposure at plasma levels in the human range tests clobazam under realistic maintenance, narrowing D15
transfer_breakers: Combination design: clobazam alone under subchronic exposure is not separated; n 6 for the threshold arm

intervention: cannabidiol; fenfluramine; lorcaserin; stiripentol; valproate; phenobarbital; clonazepam; lacosamide; rufinamide; topiramate; retigabine
control: vehicle in same mice, cross-over
effect_note: none raised the threshold significantly (retigabine p 0.86); fenfluramine and lorcaserin were null in mouse despite activity in the fish; Kv7 opener NULL here
locator_quote: hyperthermia‐induced seizures in this model of DS are highly refractory to a battery of ASDs.

transfer_breakers: Retigabine single dose and pharmacokinetics in young mice not matched; a threshold null does not exclude an effect on bursting in a GoF or excitatory-gain lesion (D22, D23)

control: vehicle in same mice; lamotrigine single dose null, sub-chronic lowered threshold

locator_quote: a significantly lowered temperature threshold as compared to vehicle‐treated mice was observed
transfer_conditions: Quantifies a pro-convulsant class effect in an interneuron-LoF mouse, the main LoF/GoF divergence
transfer_breakers: Mortality in two animals is toxicity entangled with the readout

control: vehicle in same mice, 3 tiagabine doses

transfer_breakers: Sedation or motor effects of tiagabine not reported in the text read; the reference list of the paper cites tiagabine-associated status epilepticus
